actions.mechanism: Customer round-robin bounds dispatch opportunities, not mean latency or equal worker-seconds.
actions.implementation: Maintain one active-customer ring. Each free worker dispatches one job from the head, then rotates it; append newly active customers.
actions.check: With C continuously backlogged customers and runtimes at most 60 seconds, verify each customer's inter-dispatch gap stays below 60(1+ceil(C/12)) seconds, excluding scheduler overhead.
actions.risk: No customer-count-independent bound exists under unlimited customer growth.

actions.action: Alternate short-job preference with oldest-job service
actions.mechanism: Short jobs get preferential turns; oldest-job turns prevent estimated-long jobs from being bypassed indefinitely.
actions.implementation: Within each customer's dispatch turns, alternate the oldest queued job and the smallest estimated-runtime job. Store one parity counter per customer.
actions.check: A job with k older queued jobs must start within 2(k+1) customer turns, despite continuous newer arrivals.
actions.risk: Bad estimates weaken latency benefits but do not remove oldest-job turns.

actions.action: Alternatively reserve three workers for guaranteed progress
actions.mechanism: A protected fair lane provides progress while nine workers favor short jobs across customers.
actions.implementation: Instead of pool-wide round-robin, assign three workers to customer round-robin with oldest-job selection; nine select estimated-shortest jobs. Atomically dequeue from shared queues.
actions.check: For C continuously backlogged customers, verify fair-lane inter-dispatch gaps below 60(1+ceil(C/3)) seconds, excluding scheduler overhead; compare short-job latency against pool-wide rotation.
actions.risk: The weaker fairness bound trades guaranteed service frequency for short-job opportunities.

actions.action: Calibrate size estimates using completed runtimes
actions.mechanism: Recent observations correct systematic prediction errors without making fairness depend on prediction accuracy.
actions.implementation: Retain only the last 100 completion records, including size and runtime. Predict using median runtime in coarse size buckets; fall back to the overall median.
actions.check: Evaluate predictions before incorporating each completion; compare absolute error against the original estimator and verify fairness bounds remain unchanged.
actions.risk: A heavy customer's samples can dominate; abrupt workload changes invalidate recent history.

actions.action: Test sustained overload and deliberately wrong estimates
actions.mechanism: Adversarial replay separates customer progress, queued-job starvation, and short-job latency.
actions.implementation: Simulate twelve nonpreemptive workers: one continuously backlogged customer submits 60-second jobs; others submit intermittent 1-second jobs and persistent mixed queues. Swap 30% of short/long estimates.
actions.check: Against FIFO, measure short-job mean/p95 wait, maximum customer dispatch gap, and oldest-job turn counts. Assert configured fairness bounds and eventual starts for tagged long jobs.
actions.risk: Finite tests support implementation checks, not a proof of starvation freedom.
